subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram inline buttons for pairing approve/deny

question: Should Telegram callback buttons be allowed to approve or deny pairing/device requests, and what scope must a Telegram-originated approval prove for DM pairing versus operator.admin browser/device approval?
rationale: The requested UX moves trust-changing approval into Telegram callback handling, while current source intentionally gives non-gateway Telegram command owners operator.pairing rather than operator.admin.

options.title: Define typed approval actions
options.body: Create reusable approval actions with request id, action, expiry, single-use handling, callback identity, durable-state checks, and existing scope enforcement before rendering Telegram buttons.

options.title: Limit to DM pairing
options.body: Add buttons only for lower-scope sender DM pairing and leave operator.admin browser/device approvals on CLI or Control UI until the broader step-up model is approved.

options.title: Defer chat approval
options.body: Keep command-copy approval until channel-aware device approvals and chat-originated step-up authorization are settled.

recommendation.title: Define typed approval actions
recommendation.body: Create reusable approval actions with request id, action, expiry, single-use handling, callback identity, durable-state checks, and existing scope enforcement before rendering Telegram buttons.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current-main routing candidate across the pairing reply, Telegram callback, and device-pair notification files.
